text: The AEB system shall be active at vehicle speeds between 10 km/h and 60 km/h.
The AEB system shall not be active below 15 km/h.
The system shall brake fast when a collision is imminent.

In the stationary target test scenario, the emergency braking phase shall reduce the vehicle speed by at least 20 km/h before the estimated point of impact, measured from the start of the emergency braking phase.
The emergency braking phase shall not start earlier than 3.0 s before the estimated time to collision.
The system shall work reliably in all weather conditions.
The system shall warn the driver at least 0.8 s before emergency braking starts.
The collision warning shall be acoustic and visual.
The driver shall be able to interrupt emergency braking by pressing the accelerator pedal.
The collision warning shall be clearly perceptible to the driver.
The system shall be automatically reactivated at the start of each engine start cycle.

Manual deactivation of the system shall require at least two deliberate actions by the driver, such as selecting a menu entry and confirming the selection, so that the system cannot be switched off by a single accidental button press.
When the system is deactivated, a constant optical warning signal shall be shown to the driver.
A failure warning signal shall be displayed within 10 s after a system failure is detected.
The system shall store a diagnostic trouble code for each detected sensor fault.
The system shall avoid false braking interventions as far as possible.
The radar sensor shall detect vehicles ahead at a distance of at least 150 m.
The failure warning signal shall be displayed within 5 s after a system failure is detected.
